findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Anchor the code-review.yaml verification to each gate expression, e.g. `grep -F 'code-review-concurrency' code-review.yaml | grep -F 'steps.triggers.outputs.include_concurrency'` AND a twin for `steps.union.outputs.include_concurrency`, rather than a bare prompt-name grep.
evidence: AC text: 'gated on steps.triggers.outputs.include_concurrency ... and ... gated on steps.union.outputs.include_concurrency ... checked by grep'
A grep matching only the prompt name would pass even if both lines shared one (wrong) gate expression
findings.finding: The code-review.yaml AC is verified by grep for the prompt name, but the material distinction between the two dispatch lines is the differing gate expression (steps.triggers.outputs.include_concurrency for round_a vs steps.union.outputs.include_concurrency for round_b); a bare grep for 'code-review-concurrency' does not prove each line is gated on the correct twin.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — 'code-review.yaml carries the code-review-concurrency dispatch line in BOTH the round_a batch ... and the round_b batch ... checked by grep'
scenarios: Both dispatch lines accidentally reference steps.triggers (or both steps.union) — grep on prompt name still passes but round_b never fires from the union step
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the single grep with two anchored greps asserting the presence of both distinct when-expressions alongside the code-review-concurrency prompt.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that the added-line scan skips the `+++` file header (mirroring the existing `---` skip on the removed-line path) so trigger tokens inside file paths cannot false-fire.
evidence: Plan: 'extend content_triggered_overlays to scan BOTH added and removed diff lines (file headers excluded)'
registry.py:332 current guard: `if not raw.startswith("-") or raw.startswith("---")` — only the `---` header is excluded; the added-line path has no `+++` guard yet
findings.finding: The plan extends content_triggered_overlays to scan BOTH added and removed diff lines, but the existing function only skips the `---` removed-file header (registry.py:332); the new added-line branch must skip the `+++` added-file header, otherwise a trigger token embedded in an added file's path (e.g. a rename to `src/lock(handler).py` or any `+++ b/...Mutex...`) false-fires. The plan's generic phrase 'file headers excluded' does not name the `+++` case for the added-line scan.
scenarios: A commit renaming/adding a file whose path contains a trigger substring produces a `+++ b/...` header line that would match and false-fire concurrency
findings.suggested_fix: In the extended content_triggered_overlays, guard added lines with `raw.startswith("+") and not raw.startswith("+++")` (and keep the existing `-`/`---` guard for removed lines) before substring-scanning line body.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Append the auto-fire parenthetical (matching deletion-impact/scope-intent) to the `concurrency` catalog line so the base prompt marks it as content-triggered, e.g. '(this overlay also fires automatically when the diff touches concurrency primitives).'
evidence: code-review-base.md:69 `deletion-impact — ... (this overlay also fires automatically on such diffs).`
code-review-base.md:70 `scope-intent — ... (this overlay fires automatically from the commit trailer ...)`
Plan edit (3) cue: `concurrency — threads, async tasks, ... file/DB locking` with no auto-fire parenthetical
Plan states concurrency is content-triggered: edit (2) extends `content_triggered_overlays` to return `concurrency`
findings.finding: The proposed `concurrency` catalog line in code-review-base.md omits the '(this overlay also fires automatically on such diffs)' parenthetical that BOTH existing content-triggered overlays (deletion-impact, scope-intent) carry — yet concurrency is itself content-triggered (it fires automatically from the token scan, per edit 2). The base reviewer's catalog uses this parenthetical as a locality cue distinguishing auto-firing overlays from model-recommended ones; omitting it for a content-triggered overlay is inconsistent instruction-locality in the LLM-facing catalog.
scenarios: The base reviewer, following the catalog convention, may redundantly recommend `concurrency` (harmless dedup) or the catalog reads inconsistently for a maintainer distinguishing auto-fired vs recommended overlays.
findings.suggested_fix: Change edit (3)'s catalog line to: `concurrency — threads, async tasks, multiprocessing, locks, channels, shared/global mutable state, file/DB locking (this overlay also fires automatically when the diff adds or removes such primitives).`
